frames.narration: A seller drops the price of listing L-7 from 24.99 to 19.99. The database commits the new price and, in the same transaction, a row in its outbox with the listing id and a version number, v412. The event is not lost even if the process dies right after.

The indexer reads the event, partitioned by listing id so one listing's changes stay in order. Only the price changed, so the text index is not touched: the indexer overwrites L-7's record in the side store, and only if v412 is newer than what is stored.
A shopper searches 'wireless earbuds' and filters to brand Acme, under 30, in stock. The API starts a 100 ms budget for the whole search and hands the query to a coordinator.

The coordinator sends the query to one copy of every shard, in parallel. Each shard applies the filters first, counts the brands and sizes over the filtered set, scores only the survivors with a text formula, and returns its best 100 with its counts.

messages.label: query to 1 copy of each shard

frames.narration: The coordinator merges the shard lists into the best 200 candidates and adds up the facet counts, so the page can say Acme (412), Brio (190) and so on, over everything that matched, not just the first page.

The re-ranker fetches current price and stock for the 200 in one batched lookup. It drops 14 that sold out after the index last saw them, checks that L-7's price of 19.99 is still under 30, and scores the rest: text score, a capped sales signal, a boost for new listings.

The top 10 go back with the facet counts. L-7 appears at position 3 with the price 19.99, the same as the database. The search took 62 ms of its 100 ms budget, and the API logs which listings were shown at which positions, for the judged-query runs and A/B tests that decide the next ranking change.
